{{nihongo|'''Yabuta Shrine'''|陽夫多神社}} is an {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=listed shrine}} (small shrine) in Baba, {{ill|Iga, Mie|Q460820|qid=Q460820}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Mie|af|Mie-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Mie|ar|ميه (محافظة)|ast|Prefeutura de Mie|az|Mie prefekturası|azb|میه اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Mié|be|Міэ|bg|Мие|bn|মিয়ে প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Mie|cdo|Mie-gâing|ce|Ми (префектура)|ceb|Mie-ken|ckb|پارێزگای میێ|cs|Prefektura Mie|cy|Mie (talaith)|da|Mie-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Mie|eo|Gubernio Mie|es|Prefectura de Mie|et|Mie prefektuur|eu|Mie (prefektura)|fa|استان میه|fi|Mien prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Mie|frr|Mie (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Mie|gl|Prefectura de Mie|hak|Mie-yen|he|מיאה (מחוז)|hi|मिऐ प्रीफेक्चर|hr|Mie (prefektura)|hu|Mie prefektúra|hy|Միե (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Mie|ilo|Prepektura ti Mie|it|Prefettura di Mie|ja|三重県|ka|მიეს პრეფექტურა|km|មីអិ(ខេត្ត)|ko|미에현|la|Mieensis|lt|Mijės prefektūra|lv|Mie prefektūra|mk|Мие (префектура)|mn|Миэ муж|mni|ꯃꯤꯏ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|मिई प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Mie|ne|मिए|nl|Mie (prefectuur)|no|Mie (prefektur)|nov|Mie Prefekture|os|Миэ|pam|Prepektura ning Mie|pl|Prefektura Mie|pnb|ضلع مائی|pt|Mie|ro|Prefectura Mie|ru|Миэ|se|Mie prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Mie|si|මියේ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Mie Prefecture|sk|Mie (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Мије|su|Préféktur Mie|sv|Mie prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Mie|tg|Префектураи Мие|th|จังหวัดมิเอะ|tl|Prepektura ng Mie|tr|Mie|tt|Ми (префектура)|uk|Префектура Міє|ur|میہ پریفیکچر|vi|Mie|war|Mie (prefektura)|wuu|三重县|zh|三重县|zh_classical|三重縣|zh_min_nan|Mie-koān|zh_yue|三重縣|qid=Q128196}}. {{nihongo|'''Yabuta Shrine'''|陽夫多神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Iga Province]].

== Overview ==
Yabuta Shrine is an ancient shrine counted both as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} and a {{ill|Kokushi genzaisha|Q118304363|qid=Q118304363|lt=Kokushi-genzai shrine}}, but its divine lineage is unclear. According to 'Tō Yabuta Jinja-ki,' while noting that the 'Engi Fudoki' is likely spurious, it records: "There was a deity on Kawaiyama in {{ill|Ahai district|Q11657437|qid=Q11657437}}, called Yabuta Myōjin; in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Senka|Q329728|qid=Q329728|lt=Takeohirokuni Oshitate no Sumeramikoto}}, year {{ill|Yang Earth Horse|Q905011|qid=Q905011}}, the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|Q2483673|qid=Q2483673}} Taga no Muraji worshiped it; the deity worshiped was {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}." Taga no Muraji were a lineage in {{ill|Taga, Shiga|Q1346747|qid=Q1346747}}, {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}}, tracing ancestry to {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858}}; thus worship of Susanoo, child of Izanagi, is plausible.

In '{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}},' Yabuta deity is treated as the Shikinaisha, while Takamatsu deity is treated as a non-Shikinaisha. In other words, Yabuta deity and Takamatsu deity are considered different. Takamatsu deity already held the rank of Senior Sixth, then in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635}} 3 (861) was promoted to Junior Fifth Lower together with Takakura deity, Awa deity, and Unane deity. In Jōgan 15, Awa deity and Unane deity were promoted again and entered the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, but Takakura deity and Yabuta deity did not advance and remained Kokushi genzaisha outside the Engishiki list. One interpretation is that the clan venerating Yabuta deity lost power in inter-clan political struggles. Takamatsu deity's lineage is also unclear, but {{ill|Kenzaburō Torigoe|Q28354686|qid=Q28354686}} inferred a {{ill|Katsuragi clan|Q11620908|qid=Q11620908|lt=Katsuragi-line}} connection, based on frequent use of the character "高" in Katsuragi-related divine names.

From these studies, identifying Takamatsu deity and Yabuta deity as the same remains questionable. In a written petition by priests of Yabuta Shrine is the statement: "In ancient times, from Kawai village (present site), about five chō east, from a place called Fujiyama, the deity was transferred to this shrine." Since Fujiyama referred to the alluvial zone of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tomoda River}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawai River}}, Yabuta deity was likely an agricultural deity worshiped there.

== Cultural properties ==
== Mie Prefecture designated intangible folk cultural property ==
* Gion Festival Negai-no-Yama rite

== Iga City designated cultural properties ==
* Bonshō (temple bell)
* Otabisho Kofun

== Festivals ==
Rites such as the Kinen festival and Gion festival are listed in [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1257927/1/85 Special Shinto Rites in Mie Prefecture].

== Anecdotes ==
* In the precincts is a dry {{ill|Well|Q43483|qid=Q43483}} called "Baba no Miyai." It is said water springs from it only on Yabuta Shrine's festival day. This parallels the "Wakasa-i" rite at {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nigatsu-dō}} in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}} and is one legend born from sacred-water belief tied to agricultural pre-harvest rites.
* At the {{ill|Otabisho|Q11489117|qid=Q11489117}} on the south side stands a {{ill|Kofun|Q1141225|qid=Q1141225}} called {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Otabisho Kofun}}, with its stone chamber exposed. The buried person is unknown and the tomb was looted.
* Multiple kofun have also been confirmed on Miyayama behind the shrine, the grove revered as {{ill|Chinju no Mori|Q11651158|qid=Q11651158}}. Together with Otabisho Kofun, they form the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miyayama Kofun Group}}. In the mountain are also medieval and Sengoku-period castle remains, and a walking route is maintained as "Yabuta Kofun no Mori."
* In {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544}} 5 (1473), {{ill|kampaku|Q1199966|qid=Q1199966}} and {{ill|Daijō-daijin|Q1157586|qid=Q1157586}} {{ill|Ichijō Kaneyoshi|Q1656375|qid=Q1656375}} visited Yabuta Shrine and composed this poem while crossing Takamatsu Bridge (once in the precincts).
{{Quotation|Unable to cross, swept by this floating world's waves; stepping on Kawai's bridge is perilous.|Ichijō Kaneyoshi|'Fuchigawa no Ki'}}
:It is said to liken the dangerous bridge during the {{ill|East Asian rainy season|Q658486|qid=Q658486|lt=samidare}} floods to the war-torn ruin of many provinces.
